Answer.description: What the user said in response to one interview question.

duration.description: Total length of the answer in seconds.
duration.title: Duration

transcript.description: Full text of the answer. Empty if the user stayed silent.
examples: I would use a hash map to count occurrences.
transcript.title: Transcript

words.description: Per-word timings in the order the words were spoken, used to compute pace and pauses. Empty when the speech-to-text source provides none.
words.title: Words

Answer.title: Answer

Evaluation.description: The grade for one answer, scored on four metrics.

clarity.description: How clearly and logically the answer is structured.

correctness.description: Whether the facts and reasoning in the answer are right.

depth.description: How far the answer goes beyond surface-level knowledge.

question_id.description: The id of the question this evaluation grades.
question_id.title: Question Id

relevance.description: How well the answer addresses the question and the role.

summary.description: Overall feedback on the answer, with the most important improvement.
examples: Strong fundamentals; next time, mention how keys affect list updates.
summary.title: Summary

Evaluation.title: Evaluation

MetricScore.description: A score for one grading metric, with the reasoning behind it.

feedback.description: One or two sentences explaining why this score was given.
examples: Correct explanation, but it skips how keys affect reconciliation.
feedback.title: Feedback

MetricScore.title: MetricScore

Question.description: One question the interviewer asks during a session.

id.description: Globally unique identifier of the question, generated when it is created.
id.title: Id

skill_id.description: Stable identifier of the skill this question tests. The same skill keeps the same id across all preparations and sessions.
skill_id.title: Skill Id

text.description: The question exactly as it is spoken to the candidate.
examples: How does React decide when to re-render a component?
text.title: Text

Question.title: Question

SessionStatus.description:
Where an interview session is in its life cycle.

- in_progress: the interview is under way and has no end time.
- completed: the interview ended. Grading may still be pending or may have failed.
- abandoned: the user left before finishing.
SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

Turn.description:
One question-and-answer exchange in an interview session.

A turn moves through the states described by TurnStatus, and the fields that
must be present depend on the state. A turn is immutable: to move it to its
next state, call `updated()`, which re-validates the result. Do not use
`model_copy(update=...)`, because it skips validation and can produce an
invalid turn.

answer.description: What the user said. Present once the user has answered.

evaluation.description: The grade for the answer. Present only when the status is graded.

grading_error.description: Short, cleaned-up reason that grading failed, not the raw provider error. Present only when the status is grading_failed.
grading_error.title: Grading Error

status.description: Where the turn is in its life cycle.

Turn.title: Turn

TurnStatus.description:
Where a turn is in its life cycle.

- awaiting_answer: the question was asked and the user has not answered yet.
- awaiting_grade: the user answered and the answer is waiting to be graded.
- graded: the answer was graded and the evaluation is attached.
- grading_failed: grading did not succeed; grading_error says why, and it can be retried.
TurnStatus.title: TurnStatus

WordTiming.description: One spoken word and when it was said within an answer.

end.description: Seconds from the start of the answer at which the word ends. Never earlier than start.
end.title: End

start.description: Seconds from the start of the answer at which the word begins.
start.title: Start

word.description: The spoken word as transcribed by the speech-to-text model.
word.title: Word

WordTiming.title: WordTiming

description:
One practice attempt at an interview: an ordered list of turns.

Many sessions can belong to the same preparation. The session is immutable:
to add a turn or change its status, call `updated()`, for example
`session.updated(turns=session.turns + (new_turn,))`.

ended_at.description: When the session ended. Present only when the status is completed or abandoned.
ended_at.title: Ended At

id.description: Globally unique identifier of the session, generated when it is created.
id.title: Id

preparation_id.description: The id of the preparation (job description and resume) this session practices.
preparation_id.title: Preparation Id

started_at.description: When the session started, as a timezone-aware UTC time.
started_at.title: Started At

status.description: Where the session is in its life cycle.

turns.description: The turns of the interview, in the order the questions were asked.
turns.title: Turns

updated_at.description: When the session last changed, used to resume or expire sessions.
updated_at.title: Updated At

title: InterviewSession
